title: Locality of the zero tester
statement: For every positive integer $n$, the tester that samples one coordinate uniformly and accepts exactly when its value is false is a local tester for the property of being the all-false string, with rate $1$. It accepts the all-false string with probability $1$, and for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ and every string whose normalized Hamming distance from the all-false string exceeds $\varepsilon$, its rejection probability is strictly greater than $\varepsilon$.
